//ServiceRole: Deliberately absent. SERVICE_ROLE must be set explicitly per deployment. PLAN §5 names 'all' as the launch configuration, but defaulting to it here would mean a deployment that forgot the variable gets a SECOND full rebuilder — and two replicas staging sitemap.xml concurrently can swap in each other's half-finished index. The role has to be stated where the replica count is stated.

Persistence.//MigrateOnStartup: Apply EF migrations on boot, serialised across replicas by a Postgres advisory lock. Set false to migrate as a separate one-shot Job (then the service needs no DDL rights).

Seo.//SiteUrl: Must match the SPA's canonical host EXACTLY. A wrong scheme or a stray www. does not fail — it publishes several hundred thousand URLs that all redirect.
Seo.//AllowIndexing: MUST be false on every non-production host (tst, staging, preview). A test deployment is a complete copy of the site at a different name; left crawlable it competes with production for its own rankings, and publishing a sitemap for it is the most effective way to make that happen. Defaults true so a PRODUCTION deploy that forgets the flag does not silently de-list the whole site — the startup log states which way it resolved, at WARNING, on every boot.
Seo.//CronInterval: The full-corpus rebuild is the correctness backstop, so this interval IS the staleness bound the service promises (PLAN §0).
Seo.//DebounceWindow: How long a burst of freshness events is coalesced before sitemap-jobs is re-projected. Bounds how long a withdrawn job stays advertised.

Thresholds.//: Mirror src/seo/facets/indexation.ts in kariyer-zamani-web. Changing one without the other puts the sitemap and the page's own robots meta tag into disagreement about the same facet, which Google resolves by trusting the tag and distrusting the sitemap.

FacetManifest.//CacheFor: The manifest only changes when the web app deploys. Caching turns 'the web app is mid-deploy' from a failed rebuild into a rebuild against the last known-good candidate set.

Seo.//DisallowedPaths: Kept short. robots.txt controls CRAWLING, not indexing — a disallowed URL can still be indexed from an external link, and because the crawler may not fetch it, it can never see the noindex that would remove it. Thin facets are handled by the count gate, never here. /cms-preview is the CMS admin's live preview, which renders UNPUBLISHED drafts on the public origin: this line only saves crawl budget, and the route de-indexes itself with noindex + prerender-status-code 404 while the gateway serves X-Robots-Tag: noindex for it.
Seo.//CacheControl: Shorter than CronInterval on purpose: Cloudflare fronts these files, and a TTL longer than the rebuild period would serve a purged job from an edge cache after the sitemap behind it had dropped it.

R2.//StagingPrefix: Must NOT match the Cloudflare /sitemap*.xml rule, or half-written files would be served to Googlebot — defeating the entire point of staging.
R2.//Compress: FALSE because Cloudflare fronts this bucket. Pre-compressing in object storage is only right when object storage is the origin the client talks to; behind a CDN it duplicates a job the edge does better (per-client brotli/gzip from one stored object) and creates an encoding hazard. Observed in production with it on: an Accept-Encoding: gzip client needed TWO gunzip passes because Cloudflare re-compressed an already-gzipped body, and a client sending none got gzip bytes with no Content-Encoding and Content-Type: application/xml. COUPLED TO THE CLOUDFLARE ROUTE: true makes the stored keys and the index children end in .xml.gz, so the /sitemap-*.xml rule must be repointed in the same change or the index becomes a list of 404s. See docs/DEPLOYMENT.md §4.

Rabbit.//inbound: These two are a CONTRACT with kariyer-freshness-service. A typo does not fail — it binds an empty exchange and this service silently stops hearing about expiries.
Rabbit.//FreshnessConsumerQueue: A DEDICATED queue. The freshness exchanges are fanout, so every subscriber gets its own copy; sharing a queue with another consumer would have the two competing and each expiry reaching only one of them.

Events.//RawJson: Everything in this estate is .NET. Turning this on would also strip the envelope the INBOUND freshness events rely on.

Garnet.//Enabled: Enabled means USABLE: true with an empty ConnectionString FAILS STARTUP on a role that purges. A purge that never happens is invisible — the job leaves the sitemap on schedule while the prerenderer keeps serving its rendered 'apply now' page until the TTL expires.

Indexing.//Enabled: Optional (PLAN §15 step 7). Off by default and honestly so: the API is quota-limited to 200 URLs/day, supports JobPosting only, and needs a service account added as an owner of the Search Console property. Enabled means USABLE — true without a readable CredentialsPath fails startup.
